tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for...'), describes scope (GPU training/inference clusters on HyperPod, ParallelCluster, EC2/EKS), explains what it adds (coverage audit, node verdicts, pre-flight checks), and ends with an explicit, pushy list of activation triggers covering symptoms users might describe without naming the domain (Xid/ECC errors, slow training, NCCL hangs, nodes in Failure/Pending, 'is my cluster ready for a multi-day run'). It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the technical scope.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS)... Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or 'is my cluster ready for a multi-day run'."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but nearly every sentence conveys project-specific facts (exact API calls, field names, thresholds, non-obvious behaviors) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. There is no filler explaining what GPUs, Xid errors, or CloudWatch are in general terms.
tests.evidence: R3. Node identity survives replacement. A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace gives the node a new instance ID in the same instance group...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data is embedded directly in the body rules rather than deferred to references/ files, including specific API call sequences, exact field names, percentage rescaling caveats, and Capacity Block termination timing tables, all inside conditional rule logic (R2-R11) that loads on every activation.
tests.evidence: R9. Capacity Blocks begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ (inventory-and-timeline.md, cluster-edge-cases.md, coverage-audit.md, nccl-nvlink-efa.md, xid-triage.md, incident-branches.md, signals-and-thresholds.md, preflight.md, report-format.md) is linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear statement of what content it holds and why/when to load it (e.g., for coverage queries, for Xid catalog, for pre-flight checks).
tests.evidence: Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node verdict evidence bar and branches A to F

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative paths rooted at 'references/', with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-stakes operations (CloudTrail lookups, coverage proof, Capacity Block timing) are given exact prescriptive steps, while broader classification and recommendation steps leave room for judgment (e.g., 'Recommend operator actions only').
tests.evidence: Query CloudTrail by event name, not by instance ID: cloudtrail.LookupEvents with LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName, AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]...

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple sources/tools could apply (e.g., GPU activity metrics), a default is given with an alternative as a fallback rather than an equal menu.
tests.evidence: Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (AWS/EC2 GPUPowerUtilization, unit Percent, or CWAgent), and EFA counters

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigative procedure (inventory, coverage audit, classification, root-cause branches, pre-flight checks) applicable to any cluster/incident, not a one-off declaration for a specific cluster.
tests.evidence: Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes... Step 1: Scope the request — account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes extensive non-obvious pitfalls woven throughout the R1-R11 rules (e.g., misleading log quiescence, node identity after replacement, percentage rescaling traps) which function as gotchas, plus a dedicated cluster-edge-cases.md reference.
tests.evidence: the time of the last kernel: line is not when logging stopped: a healthy kernel goes quiet.
